title: llm-routing-prefetch-brainstorm-jun-park
content:
PURPOSE / context:
- Quick scratchpad to capture product + infra ideas for combining routing policies with KV prefetch/prefix caching to reduce tail latency and token cost.
- Follow-on from convo on #serving-runtime and notes from prod review on 2024-03-12.

PROBLEM STATEMENT (rough):
- Many customers have bursty chat workloads with repeated prefixes (e.g., system prompts, few-shot examples).
- Current caching helps prefix reuse, but cold starts and cross-model routing cause misses and extra tokens.
- We need a policy layer that:
  * routes requests to the best-fitting model/variant for latency/cost
  * triggers proactive KV prefetch for predicted sessions or routes
  * gracefully falls back when prefetch fails or capacity constrained

PRD-ish goals (rough):
- Reduce median and p95 token compute by 10-30% for targeted workloads (customer A/B test).
- Reduce p95 latency for multi-turn chat by 15% in 2-week pilot.
- No user-visible correctness regressions (define via eval set).

USER STORIES (examples):
- As an app developer, I want requests with known prefixes to be routed to an instance with warmed KV cache so responses are lower-latency.
- As a platform operator, I want routing decisions to consider both capacity and whether the target has a warm cache, to balance latency and throughput.
- As a product manager, I want to enable per-customer aggressive prefetch when they opt in to reduce cost.

HYPOTHESES:
- Hypothesis 1: For chat workloads with stable prefixes, opportunistic prefetch reduces per-token compute cost by ~20% due to KV reuse.
- Hypothesis 2: Routing decisions that prefer warmed nodes reduce p95 latency more than naive capacity-based routing.

SCOPE / feature components (brainstorm):
1) Routing policy extension (control plane):
   - New policy attributes: cache_warmth_score, last_prefetch_ts, estimated_prefetch_cost.
   - Policy rules: prefer nodes with warmth_score >= threshold unless cost SLA violated.
   - UI: checkbox in Console per route: "prefer warmed instances when available".

2) Prefetch orchestration (runtime + control plane):
   - Predictive triggers: on session start / known user id / url signature -> schedule prefetch on target pool.
   - Prefetch granularity: full KV for prefix vs mini-warm (top-k kv entries) -> tradeoff perf vs memory.
   - TTL/eviction policy for prefetched KV.

3) Instrumentation & telemetry:
   - Metrics: prefetch_hit_rate, prefetch_cost / token_saved, route_warmness_delta, p95 latency delta.
   - Dashboard: per-customer and per-route timeline of prefetch activity.

4) Safety / fallback:
   - If prefetch fails or target cluster overloaded -> fallback to cold run with throttled retry.
   - Circuit breaker if prefetch cost > saved tokens over window.

TECHNICAL NOTES / implementation ideas:
- Warmth score: combination of last_access_ms, KV cache size, recent hit rate. Normalize to 0-1. Stored in node metadata.
- Prefetch actor: lightweight job queue per pool that can run prefetch tasks (limit concurrency). Use existing autoscaler signals to avoid over-allocating.
- Predictive model: start with heuristics (same user/session, same route template) then iterate to an ML model if needed.
- Data plane change: tagging requests with route/session id so KV can be indexed and reused across nodes when migrated.
- Cost accounting: tag tokens spent on prefetch vs user requests in billing/analytics.

EXPERIMENT DESIGN (MVP):
- Target cohort: 5 internal beta customers + 2 public beta. Pick customers with predictable prompt prefixes (support assist, email summary).
- A/B: route-level toggle: control (no prefetch) vs experiment (prefetch enabled, prefer warmed routing).
- Metrics: token cost per request, median latency, p95 latency, prefetch overhead. Success if token cost reduces >10% and p95 latency improves >10% with no quality regressions.

OPEN QUESTIONS / risks:
- Does prefetching cause unfair load on dedicated pools for other customers? -> need tenant-aware scheduling.
- Prefetching wrong prefixes increases cost for no benefit. How to detect and penalize?
- Security: ensure prefetch doesn't leak KV across tenant boundaries. Must integrate with isolation layer.

TODOS / next steps (actionable):
- [ ] Draft a short design doc for infra review (link: CONFLUENCE-llm-routing-prefetch-2024). Priya to own. (Priya Ramesh)
- [ ] Create JIRA epic INF-2345 and break into infra/runtime/console tickets. (Jordan)
- [ ] Identify 3 beta customers; ops to reach out for opt-in. (Aisha)
- [ ] Prototype: small PoC that tags session-based requests and schedules a simple prefetch job (target: 2-week spike). (Jun)

NOTES / rough chat snippets:
- from #serving-runtime: "we see lots of repeats for the system prompt on helpdesk flows" (Mar 8).
- slack thread link: slack.com/archives/C01ABCD123/p1678000000 -> worth pasting concrete logs into confluence.

ROUGH TIMELINE (proposal):
- 2w: design + infra spike spec
- 3w: PoC prefetch actor + simple routing preference flag
- 4-6w: internal beta & telemetry

POTENTIAL METRICS / dashboards (placeholder):
- prefetch_tasks_started_per_min, prefetch_hit_rate, prefetch_tokens_billed, customer_p95_delta, route_prefers_warm_pct

END (parking lot)
- UX question: should Console expose predicted cost-savings before enabling prefetch? nice-to-have for GA.
- Long-term: integrate with Optimize for automated recommendations (e.g., suggest prefetch for routes with high repeat rate).
